authority: Operator instruction, in session on 2026-11-14: the route of tickets B01 to B04. It sets aside V14-OP2 and V14-OP8 for this lane only. It amends no constitutional rule (CLAUDE.md section 14), closes no gate, changes no stack and changes no code pin.
decided_by: The operator chose the route in session on 2026-11-14 and gave E5 and E7 in session the same day. The agent drafted the record from tickets B01 to B04 and wrote E5 and E7 from the operator's words, quoted in their bases.
decision: Drafts leave the host as one archive. The host serves it once, on its loopback address, through a Session Manager port-forward session to the operator's workstation. Both sides check the sha256. The host gets no internet route and no S3 write.

rules.rule: The route, as decided. The workstation's sb_fetch.ps1 makes a one-use token and a neutral archive name. It starts sb_outbound_serve.sh on the host by deploy/aws/scripts/host-run.ps1 (Run Command, as root). The host packs /root/sb/outbound into one archive and serves it once at http://127.0.0.1:<port>/<token>/<archive> until one complete GET or the window ends, then deletes it. The workstation fetches through an AWS-StartPortForwardingSession session. No stack changes, no internet route, no S3 write.
rules.basis: Operator, in session, 2026-11-14. Tickets B01 and B02; tests/test_stageb_outbound_tunnel.py on the workstation. The live route is B04.

rules.rule: What proves delivery. The workstation's record: kept true, which needs the sha256 and the size to equal the host's and the host's RESULT=expected. The host's served=yes and RESULT=expected mean every byte was sent, not received. TCP cannot show more, and on Windows a client was seen cut off after the host printed them.
rules.basis: Operator decision 'Narrow the claim', in session, 2026-11-14; B01 comments; commit 0d8d7a41.

rules.rule: Where it lands. A private folder on the operator's workstation, outside every checkout and outside any cloud-synced folder. sb_fetch.ps1 refuses a folder under this repository or inside any git work tree. It does not detect a cloud-synced folder, so that part rests on the operator.

Who receives the drafts next, and by which channel. The operator only, by the SB-T2 fetch, with -Dest set to the private folder of E6. The fetch writes the archive there directly, so it needs no download folder and no move. No onward channel to anyone else is decided (G7).

known_gaps.gap: The session's content is protected by TLS and is not additionally encrypted with the project key. Inferred from E8: no session preferences document exists (evidence_v2/V14/V14_H01_session-preferences.json), so no KMS key is set for session data.
CloudTrail records each StartSession with its document name, not what was carried.

The token travels as an export line in the Run Command's commands parameter. The account's Run Command history keeps that parameter, and the SSM Agent writes the script under its own folder on the host. The token is used once and dies with the window, so a copy found later opens nothing.

Not yet shown on a real host: that the operator's role may start a port-forward session, that the SSM Agent reaches a server bound to 127.0.0.1, and how long a whole fetch takes. The fetch record's end_utc minus start_utc includes Run Command start-up, polling and clean-up, so it is not a throughput measure. B04 shows them, on an invented file.
The symlink, FIFO and SIGTERM refusals of B01 have run only in tests that skip on Windows. Their first run is on the Linux host.
A5 (processing authority for the 2026 inputs) and A7 (the RAISE DN opt-in) of gap G2 of the first lane record stay open. They get their own records.

No channel is decided for drafts to go beyond the operator, for example to the consortium. The handoff's A6 says drafts must reach the consortium. That step needs its own record before any draft leaves the private folder.
